words.gloss: only to those of such nature

literal: The crow, without concealing, calling out eats; prosperity also to such natured people only exists.
translation: Crows do not hide their food but call out to their kind to share it; prosperity likewise abides only with those who possess such a sharing nature.
modern: காகம் தனக்குக் கிடைத்த உணவை மறைக்காமல் தன் சுற்றத்தைக் கூவி அழைத்து உண்ணும். அது போன்ற பகிர்ந்துண்ணும் குணம் உடையவர்களுக்கே செல்வமும் சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the simple, everyday behavior of a crow to teach a profound lesson on cherishing one's kinsmen. The word 'கரவா' means without hiding or keeping secrets, and 'கரைந்து' refers to the crow's habit of cawing to summon its flock when it finds food. The poet states that 'ஆக்கம்' (wealth or prosperity) will only come to and stay with ('உள') those who share the crow's generous nature ('அன்ன நீரார்க்கே'). True prosperity does not belong to the selfish, but to those who actively call upon their relatives and community to share in their good fortune.
